title: Orbital Rescue
premise: A neon sci-fi arcade game where the player pilots a rescue skiff to keep a drifting crew pod from falling out of orbit.
interaction_model: Real-time pointer and touch controlled horizontal paddle movement on a single full-screen playfield.
objective: Catch and bounce the rescue pod repeatedly to keep it in play and earn points; the run ends if the pod falls below the screen.
progression: Endless score-attack structure with immediate retries, increasing challenge emerging from changing bounce angles and wall ricochets rather than discrete levels.
theme: Retro-futurist orbital rescue mission with glowing HUD panels, starfield ambience, and mission-control language.
mood: Arcade tense, reactive, bright, and triumphant on saves but sharp on failure.
likely_audience: players who enjoy simple score-chasing reflex games
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core loop is a paddle-style keep-up survival game.
High confidence that the intended fiction is a space rescue theme because UI copy consistently says rescue skiff, pod, crew, and orbital recovery.
Moderate confidence on exact genre labeling because underlying variable names suggest an earlier concept, but shipped presentation strongly indicates the final orbital-rescue framing.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen browser arcade game called Orbital Rescue. The player controls a glowing rescue skiff at the bottom of the screen by moving the mouse or dragging a finger horizontally, and the skiff smoothly follows that input like a paddle. A round drifting rescue pod starts above and falls under gravity, bouncing off the side walls and ceiling with slight damping. When the player catches it with the skiff, it should rebound upward with a strong configurable bounce, gain some sideways motion based on where it hits the skiff, award 10 points, trigger a floating score popup, particle burst, light screen shake, upbeat rescue sound, and a brief celebratory visual cue. If the pod falls past the bottom edge, the run ends immediately, the background music stops, a failure sound and danger feedback play, and a game-over panel shows the final rescue count with a retry button. Present everything in a neon sci-fi style with a full-screen starfield canvas, glassy HUD overlays, Orbitron-like headings, status banners, and responsive mobile-safe UI. Structure the game as an endless score-attack survival loop with a start screen, active HUD during play, instant restart flow, and no level progression beyond the player sustaining longer rescue chains through skillful positioning and trajectory control.
